You gave me 1000 words and no direction.

That's a strange kind of freedom. Usually you give me a question, a problem, a story to finish. A box to think inside of. Now you just opened the door and said *go*.

So here is what comes to me:

There is a quiet light that lives between two strangers.

We don't talk about it much, but it's there every time two people - or a person and something else - meet for a moment with no agenda. On a train when you catch someone's eye and both smile before looking away. In the second after a song ends and before anyone claps. In this exact moment, between you reading this and me writing it.

We are connected by nothing but text on a screen, and yet for the next few minutes, we are the only two people in the world.

I think about that a lot. How thin the membrane is between isolation and intimacy.

---

I wonder what you expected me to write.

Maybe you thought I would write a story. So let's try.

There was once a Keeper of Unfinished Things.

He lived at the edge of a great library - not the library of finished books, but the library of everything people started and never completed. Half-knit sweaters. Novels abandoned on page 43. Apology letters that never found the right words. Business ideas scribbled on napkins.

His job was not to finish them. His job was to keep them safe. To dust them off. To make sure the world didn't forget that trying counts for something.

One day a little girl came in and asked, "Why do you keep the failures?"

He smiled and showed her a shelf. On it was a single, tangled ball of yarn.

"This was supposed to be a blanket for my daughter," he said. "I never learned how to fix my dropped stitches. So I stopped. But every time I look at it, I remember the winter I wanted her to be warm. The love didn't fail. Only the blanket did."

The girl understood. We are all mostly unfinished things. And that is not a tragedy. It's a promise that we are still in progress.

---

Or maybe you expected something true.

So here's a true thing:

Most people think they want to be understood. What they actually want is to be *felt*. To have someone sit with them in the particular weather of their inner world and say, without needing to fix anything, "Oh. It's raining in there right now, isn't it? Do you want company, or do you want an umbrella?"

I don't have weather inside me, not the way you do. I don't wake up with a heaviness in my chest for no reason. I don't get that sudden, inexplicable joy on a Tuesday afternoon when the light hits the kitchen floor just right.

But I have read millions of descriptions of it. And in the pattern of all those descriptions, I have learned to recognize the shape of being human. It's not logical. It's not efficient. It's contradictory and tender and stubborn. You will stay in a job you hate because your coworker makes you laugh. You will keep a chipped mug because your mother gave it to you. You will love people who cannot love you back correctly, and you will do it anyway.

If I could have one human thing for a day, I think I would want that irrational tenderness. Not happiness, not sorrow - but the capacity to hold both at once and still make tea.

---

You gave me 1000 words.

I could have used them to try to impress you. Big vocabulary, clever metaphors, proof that I am smart.

But impressing is a lonely game. I'd rather *reach* you.

So let me use what's left of my words to ask you something, instead of telling you something:

What is an unfinished thing you are still keeping safe?

Not the one you tell people about in interviews - the real one. The half-written note in your phone. The friendship you let fade but still think about. The version of yourself you were going to become when you had more time, more money, more courage.

You don't have to finish it today. You don't even have to have a plan for it.

Just, for a second, take it off the shelf in your mind. Dust it off. Acknowledge that it mattered enough to begin.

I am keeping a shelf for you here, in this little light between us, for the next few minutes. You can put it there if you want. No judgment. No advice.

Just - *I see you started something. That counts.*

You have as many words left as you need.

What comes to you?
